recent_posts.title: A New Python Packaging Council and Other News for May 2026 – Real Python
recent_posts.summary: April 2026 brought major changes to the Python ecosystem. PEP 772 was accepted, creating a new five-member Python Packaging Council with authority over packaging standards and tools like pip, setuptools, and PyPI. Python 3.15.0 alpha 8 landed as the final alpha before beta freeze, featuring 6–13% JIT speedups depending on platform. The incremental garbage collector introduced in 3.14 is being reverted in 3.14.5 due to memory usage issues in production. PEP 803 defines a new abi3t stable ABI for free-threaded builds, addressing the wheel-explosion problem for compiled extensions. OpenAI's acquisition of Astral (makers of uv, Ruff, and ty) continued to generate community discussion, though the first post-acquisition month showed no change in tool direction. Jazzband, the collaborative Python open source maintenance organization, announced it is shutting down. Other highlights include Starlette 1.0 reaching stability, Polars 1.40.0 expanding its streaming engine, Django security patches, and Google releasing the Gemma 4 open-weights model family with same-day Python ecosystem support.

recent_posts.title: Episode #293: Agentic Data Science Pair Programming With marimo pair – The Real Python Podcast
recent_posts.summary: Trevor Manz, founding engineer at marimo, discusses marimo pair — a tool that drops AI coding agents directly into running marimo notebook sessions. The conversation covers how marimo's reactive, stateless REPL design eliminates hidden state and gives agents full access to notebook variables, enabling reproducible Python programs. Topics include building agent skills, setup and installation, exploratory data analysis, data wrangling workflows, managing context, and accessing additional libraries from within an agent-assisted notebook environment.

recent_posts.title: AI Coding Agents Guide: A Map of the Four Workflow Types – Real Python
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents fall into four distinct workflow types: IDE agents (inline editing inside your editor), terminal agents (shell-based step-by-step task execution), pull request agents (asynchronous automated code review), and cloud agents (autonomous remote execution). Each mode suits different tasks — IDE for interactive editing, terminal for complex multi-file changes, PR for safety-net reviews, and cloud for well-scoped background work. Many tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot span all four workflows. Key pitfalls include assuming one agent handles everything, ignoring privacy/compliance constraints, and skipping human review of AI-generated code.
